summary: Minute-bound 429 spikes for long-lived SSE clients caused by TLS session rekey accounting at edge
description: Customer reports periodic bursts of 429 throttles that align to minute boundaries when many telemetry clients maintain long-lived Server-Sent Events (SSE) connections. Traffic pattern: large fleet of small SSE connections (~2000 concurrent), each emits keepalive pings. Bursts last ~30-45s every minute and correspond with quota depletion on the tenant despite steady total request rate. Customer is on a dedicated pool and seeing user-facing degradation (failed SSE updates).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open ~2000 concurrent SSE connections to /v1/events (client simulation script provided).
2) Configure keepalive ping every 15s from each client and simulate periodic small POSTs for telemetry every 60s.
3) Observe per-minute sawtooth pattern in 429 rate from the client side; check quota counters in Console and edge-proxy logs.
4) Reduce keepalive to 60s or disable rekey on client to observe mitigation (workaround).
logs: Edge-proxy logs (attached) show repeated registration events for the same API key within the same minute window. Rate-limiter metrics show token consumption spikes coincident with these registrations. Sample correlation: 2026-03-09T22:14:00Z - registration event x 1800, token bucket consumption jump +4,200 units. Customer provided pcap and SSE client logs (attachments: sse_pcap_0310.gz, client_keepalive.log).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: connection churn or health-check probes consuming quota — disproved: total connection churn is low, but registration events align to minute boundaries.
Observed TLS session renegotiation/rekey events on our edge pool during the minute boundary window (TLS 1.3 key update behaviors from certain CDN front-ends).

Edge-proxy currently treats a TLS rekey as a new upstream session for rate-accounting purposes in the per-connection token attribution path, causing duplicate per-connection registration credits to be consumed when rekey occurs frequently across many concurrent SSEs.

SRE note: repro on staging with edge-proxy build 1.23.4; enabling debug exposes repeated auth handshake and API key re-evaluation at rekey. Rate-limiter increments occur before dedupe path completes, causing transient overcounting.
Correlation: customers behind specific CDN vendor X with aggressive TLS key-update intervals (default 60s) show the pattern; customers behind other CDNs do not reproduce.
Workaround verified: pinning client TLS key-update to >300s or enabling long-lived TLS sessions at the CDN reduced spike frequency to near zero in customer tests.

workaround: Customer-temporary: Configure CDN to extend TLS key-update interval (>300s) or adjust origin keepalive to reuse the same TLS session. Support recommendation: enable route separation for telemetry endpoints so they get a dedicated burst pool while we fix counting logic.
resolution: Patched edge-proxy to treat immediate post-TLS-rekey auth checks as idempotent for token accounting (dedupe window 10s). Canary rolled 2026-03-12 to 3 nodes in us-west-2 and monitored for 24 hours: 429 burst rate dropped to baseline. Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-13. Post-deploy: customer confirmed no further minute-bound spikes.
postmortem_followup: Create runbook entry for TLS-rekey-induced-accounting and add detection alert in Console if per-minute sawtooth pattern and repeated registration signatures observed. Assigned INT-4321 for longer-term robust dedupe in the auth path.
notes_for_engineering: Edge team: review auth re-eval timing and consider moving token consumption commit to after dedupe completes. Platform: add telemetry to surface key-update rates per CDN vendor as a diagnostic dimension in Console.
